outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity (LLC or corporation) with the California Secretary of State and obtain an Employer Identification Number (EIN) from the IRS. What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online through the California Secretary of State bizfile portal. Within 90 days file the Statement of Information ($20 for an LLC). Apply for the EIN online at irs.gov the same day the entity is formed; it is issued immediately and is needed for the bank account, seller's permit and business registration. Make the lease contingent on approval of the health permit and ABC licence.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for the California Seller's Permit with CDTFA and for employer payroll taxes with the California Employment Development Department. What to say: Register for the seller's permit online at cdtfa.ca.gov; it is free and often issued the same day. ABC will not process a licence application until the seller's permit exists. Register as an employer with EDD within 15 days of the first payroll; the online registration takes 1 to 7 days. Subscribe to workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or the State Compensation Insurance Fund before hiring employees.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Register the business with the San Francisco Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector and file the Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk. What to say: Apply for the Business Registration Certificate online at sftreasurer.org within 30 days of starting business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts ($55 to $700) and the certificate is issued within 1 to 5 days. The registration year runs April 1 to March 31. File the FBN statement in person or by mail with the County Clerk, then publish it in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days. Every other city department asks for the Business Account Number, so complete this immediately.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit construction plans for Department of Public Health plan check and apply for the building permit with the Department of Building Inspection. What to say: Hire an architect licensed in California who has completed restaurant projects in San Francisco to prepare plans showing the kitchen layout, equipment, finishes, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, mop sink, food-prep surfaces, restroom upgrades and any structural or mechanical changes. Submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, and the menu to DPH through the online portal; the 2026–27 plan-check fee is $828 to $2,207 depending on scope. File the building permit application with DBI at the same time and ensure 'health' is a routing station. Schedule a DPH pre-final inspection at 80 percent construction completion and a final inspection at least two weeks before opening. Install a grease interceptor per SFPUC FOG program requirements and submit the Installation Verification Form for a sewer-bill discount.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain the Certified Food Protection Manager certificate and California Food Handler cards for all employees. Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler card within 30 days of hire by completing an online ANSI-accredited course ($7 to $15, valid 3 years). DPH asks for the manager certificate at the pre-opening inspection.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the Health Permit to Operate at least one month before the planned opening date. What to say: Submit the permit-to-operate application online at sfdph.org/ehsportal with the Business Account Number, Location ID and federal tax ID; the 2026–27 application fee is $470 and the annual licence fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28. Provide proof that a certified food safety manager is on staff. The permit is issued after the final DPH inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and all equipment is installed and operational. Schedule the final inspection at least two weeks before opening; failed inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) delay openings by 2 to 3 weeks.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete Responsible Beverage Service training for all alcohol servers and managers, obtain music-licensing agreements, and apply for the sign permit if installing exterior signage. What to say: Every alcohol server and manager must complete RBS certification within 60 days of hire by registering on the ABC RBS Portal ($3), completing an approved course ($10 to $25) and passing the exam. Sign up for ASCAP and BMI public-performance licences online ($300 to $2,500 per year each, formula-based on occupancy and music use) before playing recorded music; both catalogues are required for a general mix. If installing new exterior signage, submit a sign-permit application to Planning and DBI; the fee is $300 to $1,500 and approval typically takes 7 to 45 days. Subscribe to organics collection service (green bin) with the city's hauler to comply with SB 1383 before opening.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 14 to 45 days. Estimated government cost: $470 to $1,000. Notes: The day and cost ranges shown are for the one approval the rules found to be allowed: the health permit to operate. The catalog entry for that permit gives 14 to 45 days from application to issuance after the final inspection, and the 2026–27 application fee is $470 (the annual licence fee for restaurants is $0 for 2026–28, so the maximum government cost shown is $1,000 to include potential reinspection fees). This is a time to approval, not to a denial or withdrawal. No timeline or cost is given for the other three approvals (zoning and use, alcohol licence, building permit and change of use) because the rules could not decide their status due to missing inputs; once those inputs are provided, the timelines and costs for those approvals can be calculated from the catalog entries for an ABC Type 41 licence (60 to 120 days, $1,000 to $1,600, longer if a Public Convenience or Necessity finding is required), a building permit (14 to 120 days, $800 to $15,000 depending on construction valuation), and potentially a conditional use authorization if the floor area exceeds 2,500 square feet or the business is formula retail (120 to 300 days, $3,100 to $15,000). The overall timeline to open will be driven by the building permit and ABC licence, not the health permit, but the health permit is the only approval whose status the records establish.
